--- title: "Module 10: Survey Sampling" subtitle: "Estimation with Stratified Random Sampling and Determining Sample Size" format: revealjs: # theme: simple # other modern-ish options: dark, simple, solarized theme: simple slide-number: c/t # chalkboard: true # lets you draw on top of slides (keyboard: c) or open a board (b) width: 1200 height: 675 css: modern-slides.css auto-stretch: false html-math-method: mathjax html-table-processing: none execute: warning: false message: false echo: true include-in-header: --- ::: {.cell} ::: # Estimation with Stratified Random Sampling ## Stratified Random Sampling ![](_images/10.2-stratified.png){width=60%} ## Notation for Stratified Random Sampling $N$: population size (number of sampling units in the population) $n$: sample size $L$: number of strata $N_{g}$: number of sampling units in stratum $g$ $n_{g}$: number of units **selected** from the $N_{g}$ sampling units in stratum $g$ (strata $g$'s sample size) ## Notation for Stratified Random Sampling $y_{gi}$: value of the $i^{th}$ unit in stratum $g$ **population parameters** $\mu_g$: population mean of stratum $g$ $\tau_g$: population total of stratum $g$ $\sigma^2_g$: population variance of stratum $g$ **sample statistics** $\bar{y}_g = \frac{1}{n_g}\sum_{i = 1}^{n_g} y_{gi}$: sample mean for stratum $g$ $s^2_g$: sample standard deviation of stratum $g$ ## Target Population Parameters $$ \begin{align} \tau &= \sum_{g=1}^L \sum_{i=1}^{N_g} y_{gi}\\ &= \sum_{g=1}^L \end{align} $$ $$ \begin{align} \mu &= \frac{1}{N}\tau\\ &= \frac{1}{N}\sum_{g=1}^L\qquad\mu_g \end{align} $$ ## Estimating the Population Mean with Stratified Random Sampling - Overall population mean: $\mu = \frac{1}{N}\cdot\tau$ - Overall population total: $\tau = \displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L \tau_g$ - Since the sample in each stratum is a SRS, we know that $\hat{\tau}_g = N_g\bar{y}_g$ is an unbiased estimator for $\tau_g$ - Therefore, an unbiased estimator ($\bar{y}_{st}$) for $\mu$ is: $\bar{y}_{st} = \frac{1}{N}\displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L$ ## Estimating the Population Mean with Stratified Random Sampling $$\bar{y}_{st} = \frac{1}{N}\displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L N_g\bar{y}_g$$ $$\hat{\mathbb{V}}[\bar{y}_{st}] = \frac{1}{N^2}\displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L N_g^2 \Big(1-\frac{n_g}{N_g}\Big)\Big(\frac{s_g^2}{n_g}\Big)$$ ## Estimating the Population Total with Stratified Random Sampling Therefore, an unbiased estimator for $\tau$ is: $$\hat{\tau}_{st} = N\bar{y}_{st} = \displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L N_g\bar{y}_g$$ And a reasonable estimated variance is: $$\hat{\mathbb{V}}[N\bar{y}_{st}] = N^2\hat{\mathbb{V}}[\bar{y}_{st}] = \displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L N_g^2 \Big(1-\frac{n_g}{N_g}\Big)\Big(\frac{s_g^2}{n_g}\Big)$$ ## Estimating Farm Acres -- Stratified Sampling ![](_images/10.2-stratified-sample-counties.png){width=60%} ## Estimating Farm Acres -- Stratified Sampling ::: {.cell} ::: :::columns :::column ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} table(agpop$region) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` NC NE S W 1054 220 1382 422 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(343) agpop_strat <- agpop |> group_by(region) |> mutate(N_g = n()) |> slice_sample(prop = 300/3078) ``` ::: ::: :::column ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} agpop_strat |> group_by(region, N_g) |> summarize(n_g = n(), ybar_g = mean(acres92mil, na.rm = T), sd_g = sd(acres92mil, na.rm = T)) |> knitr::kable(digits = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |region | N_g| n_g| ybar_g| sd_g| |:------|----:|---:|------:|-----:| |NC | 1054| 102| 0.340| 0.280| |NE | 220| 21| 0.102| 0.092| |S | 1382| 134| 0.186| 0.230| |W | 422| 41| 0.705| 0.702| ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Estimating Mean and Total Farm Acres -- Stratified Sampling :::columns :::{.column width=60%} $\bar{y}_{st} = \frac{1}{N}\displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L N_g\bar{y}_g$




$\hat{\tau}_{st} = N\bar{y}_{st} =$ ::: :::{.column width=40%} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} agpop_strat |> group_by(region, N_g) |> summarize(n_g = n(), ybar_g = mean(acres92mil, na.rm = T), sd_g = sd(acres92mil, na.rm = T)) |> knitr::kable(digits = 3) |> kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 25) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
region N_g n_g ybar_g sd_g
NC 1054 102 0.340 0.280
NE 220 21 0.102 0.092
S 1382 134 0.186 0.230
W 422 41 0.705 0.702
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Estimating Variability of Estimated Farm Acres :::columns :::{.column width=60%} $\hat{\mathbb{V}}[\bar{y}_{st}] = \frac{1}{N^2}\displaystyle\sum_{g = 1}^L N_g^2 \Big(1-\frac{n_g}{N_g}\Big)\Big(\frac{s_g^2}{n_g}\Big)$




$\hat{\mathbb{V}}[\hat{\tau}_{st}] =$ ::: :::{.column width=40%} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} agpop_strat |> group_by(region, N_g) |> summarize(n_g = n(), ybar_g = mean(acres92mil, na.rm = T), sd_g = sd(acres92mil, na.rm = T)) |> knitr::kable(digits = 3) |> kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 25) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
region N_g n_g ybar_g sd_g
NC 1054 102 0.340 0.280
NE 220 21 0.102 0.092
S 1382 134 0.186 0.230
W 422 41 0.705 0.702
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Using `R` for Sampling Estimates - `survey` package ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(survey) ``` ::: **Step 1: Set Up Design** :::columns :::column **SRS** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} srs_des <- svydesign(id = ~1, data = agpopsrs, fpc = ~N, na_weights = "warn") ``` ::: ::: :::column **Stratified** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} strat_des <- svydesign(id = ~1, data = agpop_strat, strata = ~region, fpc = ~N_g, na_weights = "warn") ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Using `R` for Sampling Estimates - `survey` package **Step 2: Estimates** :::columns :::column **SRS** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # mean or prop svymean(~acres92mil, design = srs_des, na.rm = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mean SE acres92mil 0.2937 0.0259 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # total svytotal(~acres92mil, design = srs_des, na.rm = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` total SE acres92mil 897.95 79.17 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::column **Stratified** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # mean or prop svymean(~acres92mil, design = strat_des, na.rm = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mean SE acres92mil 0.30328 0.019 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # total svytotal(~acres92mil, design = strat_des, na.rm = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` total SE acres92mil 927.24 58.297 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## What if we used the wrong design for estimation? :::callout-warning ## Wrong analysis -- ignoring strata in estimation ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} incorrect_des <- svydesign(id = ~1, data = agpop_strat, fpc = ~N, na_weights = "warn") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # mean or prop svymean(~acres92mil, design = incorrect_des, na.rm = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mean SE acres92mil 0.30359 0.0212 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # total svytotal(~acres92mil, design = incorrect_des, na.rm = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` total SE acres92mil 928.17 65.026 ``` ::: ::: ::: # Determining Sample Size ## Extension: Estimating Population Proportions - We haven't talked about estimating population proportions yet... - This is because a **proportion** is just a special **mean** where the outcome variable is **binary** $$ y_i = \begin{cases} 1 & \quad \text{if ``success"}\\ 0 & \quad \text{if ``failure"} \end{cases} $$ **SRS:** $p = \frac{1}{N}\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^N y_i = \frac{\text{\# successes}}{N} \qquad \qquad \hat{p} = \frac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^n y_i = \frac{\text{\# successes}}{n}$ ## Review: Population Proportions Population: - $p$ is the population proportion of successes - $\sigma^2 = p(1-p)$ is the population variance Sample: - $\hat{p}$ is the sample proportion of successes - $\mathbb{E}[\hat{p}] = p$ - In previous classes with infinite populations: $\mathbb{V}[\hat{p}] = \frac{p(1-p)}{n}$ ## Estimating Population Proportions **SRS** | Estimator | | |---------------|-----| | Point | $\hat{p} = \bar{y} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^ny_i$| | Variance | $\hat{\mathbb{V}}(\hat{p}) = \Big(1 - \frac{n}{N}\Big)\frac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n-1}$ | : {tbl-colwidths="[10,50]"} **Stratified** | Estimator | | |---------------|------------| | Point | $\hat{p}_{st} = \bar{y}_{st} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{g=1}^LN_g\hat{p}_g$ | | Variance | $\hat{\mathbb{V}}(\hat{p}_{st}) = \frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{g=1}^LN_g^2\Big(1 - \frac{n_g}{N_g}\Big)\frac{\hat{p}_g(1-\hat{p}_g)}{n_g-1}$ | : {tbl-colwidths="[10,50]"} ## Review: Confidence Intervals $$\hat{\theta} \pm \text{critical value} \times SE(\hat{\theta})$$ 95% CI: $\hat{\theta} \pm 2 \times SE(\hat{\theta})$ ## Bound on Error of Estimation Simple Random Sampling for population mean: $$B = 2\sqrt{\Big(\frac{N-n}{N-1}\Big)\frac{\sigma^2}{n}}$$ Stratified Random Sampling for population mean: $$B = 2\sqrt{\sum_{g=1}^L \Big(\frac{N_g}{N}\Big)^2 \Big(\frac{N_g-n_g}{N_g-1}\Big)\frac{\sigma_g^2}{n_g}}$$ ## Determining Sample Size - Big Idea $$B = 2\sqrt{\Big(\frac{N-n}{N-1}\Big)\frac{\sigma^2}{n}}$$ $$\hat{y} \pm B$$ ## Calculating Sample Size - SRS Sample size required to estimate the population **mean**, $\mu$, or **total**, $\tau$ with a bound on the error of estimation $B$: $$n = \frac{N\sigma^2}{(N-1)D + \sigma^2}$$ where $$D = \frac{B^2}{4} \text{ when estimating } \mu$$ $$D = \frac{B^2}{4N^2} \text{ when estimating } \tau$$ ## Calculating Sample Size - SRS Sample size required to estimate the population **proportion** $p$ with a bound on the error of estimation $B$: $$n = \frac{N p(1-p)}{(N-1)D + p(1-p)}$$ where $$D = \frac{B^2}{4} \text{ when estimating } p$$ ## Calculating Sample Size - Stratified Random Sampling Multi-step process: 1. Determine how you want to *allocate* the sample size between clusters $$n_g = a_g n \qquad \text{ for } g = 1, ..., L \text{ and } a_1 + ... + a_L = 1$$ $$a_g\text{ is the proportion of sampling units allocated to stratum }g$$ 2. Determine the overall sample size $n$ given a bound $B$ 3. Calculate the appropriate stratum sizes $n_1, ..., n_L$, given $n$ and the chosen allocation ## Calculating Sample Size - Stratified Random Sampling *Approximate* sample size required to estimate the population **mean**, $\mu$, or **total**, $\tau$ with a bound on the error of estimation $B$: $$n = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^L N_g\sigma_g^2/a_g}{(N-1)D + \sigma^2}$$ where $a_g$ is the fraction of observations *allocated* to stratum $g$ and $$D = \frac{B^2}{4} \text{ when estimating } \mu, \quad D = \frac{B^2}{4N^2} \text{ when estimating } \tau$$ ## Stratified Random Sampling -- How to Choose Allocation? Consider three factors: 1. $N_g$: 2. $\sigma^2_g$: 3. $c_g$: Cost of obtaining an observation in each stratum Three types of allocations: - Proportional Allocation - Optimal Allocation - Neyman Allocation ## Proportional Allocation - number of sampled unit in each stratum is proportional to the size of the stratum. $$a_g = \frac{N_g}{N} \quad \quad n = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^L N_g\sigma_g^2}{ND + \displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^L\frac{N_g}{N}\sigma_g^2}$$ $\pi_{gi} =$ - Use when: cost of sampling and variances are approximately equal for all strata ## Optimal Allocation - Increases precision if stratum variances vary across strata - minimizes variance for a fixed total cost or - minimizes cost for a fixed variance (i.e. fixed B) $$a_g = \frac{N_g\sigma_g^2/\sqrt{c_g}}{\sum_{h = 1}^L N_h\sigma_h/\sqrt{c_g}} \quad \quad n = \frac{\Big(\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^L N_g\sigma_g/\sqrt{c_g}\Big)\Big(\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^L N_g\sigma_g\sqrt{c_g}\Big)}{N^2D + \displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^LN_g\sigma_g^2}$$ - Use when: costs of sampling and stratum variances vary across strata ## Neyman Allocation - special case of optimal allocation when costs are similar between strata - will support more precise estimation than proportional allocation if stratum variances are specified correctly $$a_g = \frac{N_g\sigma_g^2}{\sum_{h = 1}^L N_h\sigma_h} \quad \quad n = \frac{\Big(\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^L N_g\sigma_g\Big)^2}{N^2D + \displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^LN_g\sigma_g^2}$$ - Use when: stratum variances vary across strata *but* costs of sampling are the same ## Determining Sample Size and Allocation for Estimating Proportions - Remember, the population proportion $p$ and sample proportion $\hat{p}$ are just special cases of means where $y$ is a binary variable. - Follow the equations for estimating the population mean $\mu$ but **substitute** - for the overall population variance: $p(1-p) = \sigma^2$ - for a stratum population variance: $p_g(1-p_g) = \sigma_g^2$ ## Summary of Allocations - **Proportional** Allocation - Cost of sampling **and** variances are approximately **equal** for all strata - Size (either), Variability (equal), Cost (equal) - Usually do this! - **Optimal** Allocation - Costs of sampling **and** stratum variances **vary** across strata - Size (equal), Variability (VARY), Cost (VARY) - **Neyman** Allocation - **only costs** of sampling **vary** across strata - Size (either), Variability (VARY), Cost (equal) ## Summary To determine a sample size, 1. Determine your desired maximum bound of error $B$ 2. Approximate population variance(s) using one of the options... - historical data, a pilot study, or - estimating $\mu$ or $\tau$? **last resort** $\rightarrow$ (range of variable)/4 - estimating $p$? **last resort** $\rightarrow$ use $p = 0.5$ or for a conservative estimate 3. **If stratified sample**, choose allocation type 3. Calculate $n$ for the appropriate population parameter and study design, given (1) the bound you chose, (2) approximated population variances, and (3) allocations if appropriate 3. **If stratified sample**, calculate stratum sample sizes ($n_g$'s) from $n$ and allocations

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
